vulnerability.explanation: The command line is tokenized into a fixed-size array args[1024] without bounds checking (argv[argc++] = q = p;). A command line with more than 1024 tokens will write past the end of the args array on the stack. Additionally, the subsequent argv[argc] = NULL at line 386 can also write out of bounds. This can be triggered by invoking the program with many short, space-separated arguments, leading to memory corruption.
